clue.text: One way to get a rate reduction

definitions.text: One way to get a rate reduction

parts.words: One way to get a rate reduction
parts.note: reads like a tax or finance tip, but it is simply going less fast, cutting the rate of travel

explanation.surface: Advice on lowering a rate, as from a bank or council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rate' suggests interest or local taxes; here it is speed, and the reduction is easing off.
explanation.definitionFit: Easing off speed is the plainest way to cut one's rate of movement.

clue.text: Shoot the gullible one

explanation.surface: An order to fire on a naive person.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener's term for a shoot springing from a root, and slang for a person easily fooled.

clue.text: Put on gear that's uncommonly colourful

indicators.note: uncommonly means in an unusual way, so the letters are set in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dresses in strikingly bright clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncommonly' rearranges ON and GEAR; 'Put' and 'that's' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour between red and yellow, a bright shade, so loosely a colourful one.

clue.text: Punitive measure that is in keeping

explanation.surface: A punishment that is appropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in keeping' looks like 'fitting'; it means being kept in, as a pupil is after school.
explanation.definitionFit: A school punishment of staying behind, and generally the state of being held in custody.

clue.text: Not a free and 'easy way to take a dip.

definitions.text: Not a free and 'easy way to take a dip

parts.words: Not a free and 'easy way to take a dip
parts.note: describes a forced plunge into the sea, the pirate punishment of stepping off a board blindfold

explanation.surface: A remark about bathing that is far from relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take a dip' sounds like a pleasant swim; the dip is the fatal drop pirates forced on captives.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirates made prisoners step off a board over the sea, an involuntary and deadly plunge.

clue.text: Place of secret laughter

parts.note: alludes to the idiom of laughing up one's arm covering, meaning to be amused privately

explanation.surface: Somewhere people go to laugh in private.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'laugh up one's sleeve' means to be secretly amused.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom of laughing up one's arm covering makes that garment part the home of hidden amusement.

clue.text: Movement to 'dismiss 'a deity?

parts.note: a lar is a Roman household god
'go!' is the word one says to dismiss someone

explanation.surface: A gesture or campaign aimed at banishing a god.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as the order 'Lar, go!', a household god being sent away. 'Movement' is a section of a symphony, here one played slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow section of a musical work is named after its tempo marking.

clue.text: Put one lake as a retreat for solitary types

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: to put is to set
one is the Roman numeral I
a mere is a lake

explanation.surface: Building a lakeside retreat for people who like to be alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a retreat' turns SETIMERE round as a whole; the retreat looks like a hermitage.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious hermits who withdrew to live alone, often in the desert.

clue.text: Was Lauder this kind 'of orator ?

parts.note: reads the singer's surname as 'one who lauds', a speaker giving praise

explanation.surface: A question about the Scottish music-hall singer Harry Lauder's speaking style.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Harry Lauder was a famous Scottish music-hall entertainer; read 'Lauder' as a common noun, someone who lauds.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who delivers speeches of praise is one who lauds.

clue.text: Cunning way to -go to sea ?

parts.note: the adverb for slyly also reads as travelling by craft, that is by boat

explanation.surface: A crafty plan for putting to sea.
explanation.walkthrough: A craft is a boat, so going to sea by craft is done in a cunning manner too.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means slyly or with guile, cunning being its synonym.

clue.text: Severe test for an alternative to wood

parts.note: the word 'or' introduces an alternative
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: A hard trial for some substitute for timber.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is softwood timber, pine or fir, so 'or deal' offers an alternative.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful or trying experience that tests endurance.

clue.text: Training establishment, not only in Yorkshire

definitions.text: Training establishment, not only in Yorkshire

parts.words: Training establishment, not only in Yorkshire
parts.note: a place where horsemanship is taught, with a nod to the Ridings, Yorkshire's historic divisions

explanation.surface: A college found in Yorkshire and elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire was divided into three Ridings, so the name sounds Yorkshire-specific, but these exist everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: An establishment that teaches horsemanship to riders.

clue.text: The French return with spirit to marbles

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the French article is read backwards

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A Frenchman comes back with a drink to play marbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns LE into EL. The Elgin Marbles are classical sculptures from the Parthenon in the British Museum.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Elgin's name is attached to the Parthenon sculptures he brought to London, so the name stands for those carved stones.

clue.text: Business that might suit a lot of people:

definitions.text: Business that might suit a lot of people

parts.words: Business that might suit a lot of people
parts.note: a trade that makes suits, clothing for many customers, with 'suit' in its sense of please

explanation.surface: A company whose products would please many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' means please on the surface, but this trade literally makes suits.
explanation.definitionFit: The trade of making fitted clothes such as suits.

clue.text: They naturally warm to their work

definitions.text: They naturally warm to their work

parts.words: They naturally warm to their work
parts.note: 'warm to' means grow keen on, but these workers literally face heat at blazes

explanation.surface: People who are enthusiastic about their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warm to' is an idiom for coming to like; the workers here meet real heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a brigade that puts out blazes, so their work is hot.

clue.text: Airy entertainers ?

parts.note: 'airy' suggests light-hearted, but means 'of the air', as in cabin crew on planes

explanation.surface: Light-hearted performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airy' points to the air: flight attendants were called air hostesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who receive and look after guests, and in the air, cabin crew.

clue.text: Champions in making top. sales'

indicators.note: making suggests constructing something new, so the letters are reworked into another order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Star sellers who achieve the best figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in making' rearranges TOP and SALES.
explanation.definitionFit: Champions of a cause are its advocates, as the first Christian missionaries were.

clue.text: One ', more ready to help those at a loss, for words?

definitions.text: One ', more ready to help those at a loss, for words?

parts.words: One ', more ready to help those at a loss, for words?
parts.note: the comparative of 'prompt' means more ready, and the same word names the theatre helper who feeds forgotten lines

explanation.surface: Someone keener to assist the tongue-tied.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is both 'more prompt' (more ready) and the person who whispers forgotten lines to actors.
explanation.definitionFit: In the theatre this person supplies cues to actors who forget their lines.

clue.text: He can't. handle customers who lose their heads

definitions.text: He can't. handle customers who lose their heads

parts.words: He can't. handle customers who lose their heads
parts.note: 'lose their heads' means panic, but taken literally such clients leave no skull to feel

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who cannot deal with panicking clients.
explanation.walkthrough: This practitioner read character from the bumps of the skull by touch, so a client literally without a head is no use.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner of the old pseudoscience of reading character from skull shape.

clue.text: Song appropriately heard in The Rising Sun " ?

definitions.text: Song appropriately heard in The Rising Sun

parts.words: Song appropriately heard in The Rising Sun
parts.note: 'The Rising Sun' looks like a pub name, but means daybreak, when a dawn song fits

explanation.surface: A tune that suits a pub called The Rising Sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rising Sun is a common pub name; the song meant is one for dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A poem or piece of music greeting the dawn.

clue.text: Some have a long nap, some a short

definitions.text: Some have a long nap, some a short

parts.words: Some have a long nap, some a short
parts.note: 'nap' looks like a doze, but is the raised pile on woven fabric

explanation.surface: People vary in how long they doze.
explanation.walkthrough: Nap is the raised surface of fabric such as velvet, not a sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces or kinds of woven fabric, whose pile may be long or short.

clue.text: Chopin's my choice for musical arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so the preceding letters are reordered

parts.note: the composer's name with its possessive S kept as a letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone names the Polish composer as their favourite for an orchestral version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' reorders CHOPINS plus MY; 'choice for' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a large orchestral work, hence musical in character.

clue.text: Clean 'display by escapists

parts.note: alludes to the idiom 'show a clean pair of' feet backs, meaning run away fast

explanation.surface: Fugitives putting on a spotless show.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'show a clean pair of heels' means to outrun pursuers.
explanation.definitionFit: The back parts of the feet are what fleeing people show to those behind them.

clue.text: Like Shirley's sceptre, crown, scythe and spade

definitions.text: Like Shirley's sceptre, crown, scythe and spade

parts.words: Like Shirley's sceptre, crown, scythe and spade
parts.note: quotes James Shirley's poem in which royal emblems tumble down and lie in the dust level with tools of the poor

explanation.surface: A reference to symbols of royalty and labour in a poem by James Shirley.
explanation.walkthrough: James Shirley's 'The glories of our blood and state' says sceptre and crown 'in the dust be equal made' with the poor crooked scythe and spade.
explanation.definitionFit: Death levels king and labourer, so their emblems end up the same.

clue.text: Untidy little beasts

explanation.surface: Messy small animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To strew rubbish and make a place messy, and a brood of young animals born together.

clue.text: Margaret Kennedy's nymph

parts.note: refers to the title of Margaret Kennedy's 1924 bestselling novel about a faithful girl

explanation.surface: A mythical spirit created by the novelist Margaret Kennedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Kennedy's best-known novel is 'The Constant Nymph' (1924).
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective in the novel's title, meaning faithful or unchanging.

clue.text: Most 'certain to put us back with the others.

indicators.note: putting something back reverses it, so the word us is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A firm view on rejoining the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns US into SU.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a word meaning confident or certain.

clue.text: Swell watering places

parts.note: 'swell' looks like 'smart', as in fashionable spas, but is the verb: fluid-filled spots that swell on skin

explanation.surface: Fashionable spa towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' reads as an adjective for smart resorts; it is the verb, and the watery places are on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised pockets of fluid on the skin, caused by friction or burns.
